title: audio_plan.v0
description: Audio Intelligence policy. Event state describes what the picture does; mix role describes how present the sound is. The two are orthogonal and must agree with the visual evidence. Policy is validated; synthesis, mixing, and mastering are NOT_IMPLEMENTED.

vo_strategy.description: One continuous performance cut into segments is the default: the same prompt does not reliably reproduce the same sampled speaker.

water_events.description: Rules enforced by the validator: a shot without water evidence must be OFF, and a non-BED role requires an active event state.

bgm_structure.description: Must be exactly HOOK_INTRO -> PRODUCT_BUILD -> USAGE_LIFT -> CTA_RESOLVE. A single track laid end to end is not accepted.

continuity_reason.description: A sound bridge is only allowed with an explicit continuity reason.

semantic_unit.description: The binding target. A voice line binds to a semantic unit, never to a stored timestamp, so a timeline that shifts re-resolves instead of leaving the voice describing a shot that is no longer on screen.

silence_reason.description: Mandatory when required is false: a slot left without voice must state why, so a hero may be silent but never by accident.

window_seconds.description: An optional declared window, used only when the timeline cannot resolve the semantic unit.

intent.description: What the music is asked to do. Intent, not level: the executor decides the gain against the rest of the mix and reports the measured result as evidence. No gain field exists here on purpose, because concrete values belong to one job.

transition.description: RAMP is the default because an instant step is what makes music appear to drop out; a STEP is allowed only with a stated reason.

x-policy.voice_binding: semantic unit, never an absolute timestamp
x-policy.sfx_default: off unless it improves comprehension, realism, commercial emphasis or rhythm
x-policy.module_status_is_not_an_instance_field: IMPLEMENTATION is module state and is deliberately absent from this document's properties
